title: Probabilistic handoff pilot: kernel-fit scoring + attention-aware prefill probes for speculative decode
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a prototype runtime component that does probabilistic handoff for speculative decoding by combining a lightweight kernel-fit scoring heuristic with an early attention-density prefill probe. The goal is to reduce end-to-end latency and GPU token cost for common short/medium completions while keeping quality regressions bounded by strict acceptance metrics and a deterministic fallback path.

Goals:
- Implement a kernel-fit score that selects the most efficient kernel variant (quantized vs fp16, tiled vs fused) per-request using sequence-length and kv-cache footprint estimates.
- Add an attention-aware prefill probe: after N prefill tokens (configurable, default 8), compute an attention-sparsity & peakedness signal to predict whether the speculative model will be accepted.
- Combine kernel-fit and attention probe into a probabilistic handoff policy producing an acceptance probability and a calibrated confidence threshold per model variant.
- Provide a graceful fallback: when acceptance fails, reroute to guarded decode (higher-fidelity model or synchronous full decode) with defined latency and cost budgets.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype integrates with runtime routing and can be toggled per-customer via route config.
- Telemetry emits per-request: kernel_fit_score, attention_probe_score, acceptance_probability, accept_decision, fallback_reason, end_to_end_latency, tokens_charged.
- On 1M sampled short-requests workload (internal bench), we see >=6% p50 latency reduction and <=1.5% user-visible output divergence (measured against reference decode) after rollout to 10% of traffic.
- Fallback path must re-run decode without state corruption and expose metric that counts double-decode occurrences.

Implementation approach (high level):
1) Kernel-fit scoring: fast estimator using model metadata (layer sizes, KV memory per token), recent kernel performance table indexed by (model_arch, sequence_length_bucket, hardware_family). Score = estimated_tokens_ms / memory_priority_penalty. Keep estimator entirely in C++ helper used by router to avoid RPC.
2) Attention probe: lightweight attention-summary computed by running a single-head attention pass restricted to first M tokens of prefill (M default 8). Output metrics: average attention entropy, top-k mass, diagonal mass. Convert to normalized "attention_probe_score" via logistic calibration.
3) Probabilistic handoff policy: acceptance_probability = sigmoid(alpha * kernel_fit_score + beta * attention_probe_score + gamma * model_priority). Alphas/betas are config flags tuned by offline calibration job (see links).
4) Fallback & safety: route to fallback model variant when accept_decision == false or when probe indicates low confidence. Implement per-request idempotency token to ensure safe retry/re-decode if fallback chosen.
5) Configuration: expose per-route thresholds, min-traffic gating, and decay windows to avoid oscillation.

Telemetry & metrics:
- New counters/metrics: runtime.spec.handoffs.total, .accepted, .fallbacks.synchronous_decode, .double_decodes, .probe_latency_ms.
- Histograms for acceptance_probability, kernel_fit_score, attention_probe_score, end_to_end_latency_by_path.
- Dashboard: Grafana panel showing acceptance vs false-reject rate and cost delta (token-ms) per model.

Fallback playbook:
- If acceptance metrics degrade (false-accept > 0.8% or user-visible divergence > 2%), automatically throttle speculative handoff by reducing threshold and/or pause rollout.
- Alerting: PagerDuty if double_decode rate > 0.1% of requests in 5m window for production routes.
- Runbook steps: (1) revert route to deterministic decode, (2) gather telemetry bundle, (3) roll back kernel selection table if recent change.

Rollout plan:
- Start with internal beta on dedicated infra across 2 zones. Canary to 0.1% traffic, monitor for 24h. If stable, increase to 1%, then 10% with automated safety gates.
- Target release in runtime-1.20 canary window, gate by controlled feature flag and per-customer opt-in.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: probe cost outweighs benefit on very short completions. Mitigation: short-circuit probe for requests with prefill_tokens < 4.
- Risk: kernel-fit table staleness after model changes. Mitigation: background profiler job updates table weekly and on model onboard.
- Risk: correlated failures causing simultaneous fallbacks to synchronous decode and capacity spikes. Mitigation: backpressure with token-burst caps and fallback rate-limiter.

Open questions:
- Optimal M (prefill probe tokens) trade-off between signal quality and probe compute cost — initial tuning suggests 6-10 tokens.
- Should attention probe run on a specialized fast attention kernel (biased to one head) or reuse runtime attention path? (Performance trade-offs; prototype will measure both.)

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- Build C++ kernel-fit estimator and expose via runtime API (Aisha) (ETA: 2025-02-24).
- Implement attention-probe microkernel and benchmark probe cost across hardware families (Marcus) (ETA: 2025-02-26).
- Create offline calibration job to tune alpha/beta/gamma and generate initial thresholds (Data Eng) (ETA: 2025-03-03).

Notes on uniqueness: This pilot emphasizes combining a kernel cost-aware score (hardware and kv-memory sensitive) with an attention-sparsity probe performed during prefill rather than relying only on early-token logits. The policy intentionally treats acceptance as a calibrated probability so we can adjust risk appetite per-route and per-customer, and provides a deterministic, idempotent fallback to preserve correctness.
